headline: Building a RAG System from Scratch with pgvector and Gemini
summary: Learn how to implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) from the ground up, using pgvector for semantic search and Google's Gemini.
details: LLMs are powerful, but their knowledge is limited to their training data. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a design pattern that overcomes this by retrieving relevant external documents and injecting them into the LLM's context.

This guide focuses on the practical implementation of a RAG system. We'll start with the fundamentals, including text embedding to convert text into numerical vectors for semantic similarity searches.

A vector database, unlike a traditional keyword database, finds semantically related documents even if they don't share exact words. We'll be using pgvector, a PostgreSQL extension, to power our vector database.
The article series will cover building a RAG system from scratch, extending it with Tool Use, AI Agents, MCP, and finally deploying it to the cloud. This is the introductory piece to set the stage.
caption:
Unlock LLM potential beyond training data! Learn to build a RAG system from scratch using pgvector and Gemini.

LLMs are powerful, but their knowledge is limited to their training data. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a design pattern that overcomes this by retrieving relevant external documents and injecting them into the LLM's context.

This guide focuses on the practical implementation of a RAG system. We'll start with the fundamentals, including text embedding to convert text into numerical vectors for semantic similarity searches.

A vector database, unlike a traditional keyword database, finds semantically related documents even if they don't share exact words. We'll be using pgvector, a PostgreSQL extension, to power our vector database.

The article series will cover building a RAG system from scratch, extending it with Tool Use, AI Agents, MCP, and finally deploying it to the cloud. This is the introductory piece to set the stage.
